issues.source_quote: Когда это кончится?
issues.translation_quote: when will this end?
issues.justification: The film's running gag is the double meaning of 'кончится' (end / ejaculate-like innuendo in Timofeev's 'Сейчас заканчиваю'); the pun is flattened and the follow-up 'Я спрашиваю, когда кончатся ваши опыты' loses the comic effect.

issues.source_quote: Меня терзают смутные сомнения
issues.translation_quote: I'm plagued by vague suspicions
issues.justification: Famous quoted catchphrase (Bunsha/Shpak) is rendered plainly; the literary-quote register is lost, and 'doubts' is closer than 'suspicions'.

issues.source_quote: Нечистая сила! ... Вот что крест животворящий делает!
issues.translation_quote: Behold the power of the life-giving Cross!
issues.justification: Context: the tsar says this while the police-like Bunsha 'walled in' the demons; the translation is acceptable, but 'Walled in! They've walled me in' misattributes the subject (Ivan the Terrible says the demons were walled up), changing meaning.

issues.source_quote: Закусывать надо! Быстрей!
issues.translation_quote: You've got to eat something with it! Faster!
issues.justification: Mistranslation/unclear: the line is 'Time to have a bite! Hurry!' (Bunsha-turned-tsar's attendants/feast), the added 'with it' invents a reference.

issues.source_quote: Как покойники стреляют!?
issues.translation_quote: How the dead are shooting?!
issues.justification: Ungrammatical and unnatural; the humorous astonishment is garbled.

issues.source_quote: Ой, не лги! Царю лжешь! Не человечьим хотением, но Божьим соизволением царь есъм!
issues.translation_quote: Oh, lie not! Thou liest to the Tsar!
issues.justification: Archaic 'thou' register is applied inconsistently: Ivan switches between 'thou' and modern forms, and 'thou' is also given to Miloslavsky, Bunsha and others in modern-speaking scenes, undermining the contrast between the tsar and modern characters.

issues.source_quote: Ну что ж, придется повысить напряжение.
issues.translation_quote: Well then, I'll have to raise the voltage.
issues.justification: 'Напряжение' also means tension, and the song/experiment sequence plays on it; acceptable literally but the comic deadpan is lost.

issues.source_quote: Три раза я разводилась. Ну да, три. Зюзина я не считаю.
issues.translation_quote: I've been divorced three times. Well, yes, three. I don't count Zyuzin.
issues.justification: Minor loss only; but 'Никогда я так не волновалась' rendered 'nervous' is fine. (Retained as note: acceptable.)

issues.source_quote: Тьфу на Вас!
issues.translation_quote: Pfft to you!
issues.justification: Unnatural calque; natural English would be 'Oh, go on with you!' or 'Phooey on you!'. The comic exasperation fails.

issues.source_quote: Оригинальный Вы человек! ... Однако у Вас характер!
issues.translation_quote: What an unusual man you are! ... What a temperament you have!
issues.justification: Ulyana's irony and the sharp comic exchange ('Будь я Вашей женой... я бы повесился') is weakened; 'temperament' is also later reused for Zina's praise, flattening distinct lines.

issues.source_quote: Не закрывайте рот!
issues.translation_quote: Don't close your mouth!
issues.justification: Dentist-clinic joke: the patient is told not to close his mouth for the dentist; the context is lost without clarification.

issues.source_quote: Я - артист больших и малых академических театров!
issues.translation_quote: I am an actor of the big and small academic theaters!
issues.justification: The pun on Bolshoi and Maly theaters is lost; the translation should reference 'Bolshoi and Maly'.

issues.source_quote: Сказать, как Вы смотрите, отец родной? На мне узоров нету и цветы не растут.
issues.translation_quote: I've got no patterns on me and no flowers growing.
issues.justification: Rendered nearly literally; the idiom 'There are no patterns on me' (nothing to stare at) is not understandable in English.

issues.source_quote: Граждане, храните деньги в сберегательной кассе!
issues.translation_quote: Citizens, keep your money in a savings bank!
issues.justification: Soviet slogan is retained, but the culturally specific parody is not explained; adequate but unmarked. 'Savings bank' loses the Soviet 'savings office' flavour.

issues.source_quote: Трубку! ... Ложи трубку!
issues.translation_quote: Lay down the phone!
issues.justification: The joke depends on the tsar's incorrect 'ложи' versus 'положи'; the translation's 'Lay down' vs 'Put down' only partly conveys it and 'Put down what?' confuses.

issues.source_quote: Не вели казнить, Великий государь, надежа!
issues.translation_quote: Order not my execution, great sovereign, our hope!
issues.justification: Stiff, unidiomatic rendering of the formulaic plea 'Do not order me executed / Forgive me, sire'; 'надежа' (dear hope-sovereign) is awkward.

issues.source_quote: Шайбу, шайбу...
issues.translation_quote: Goal, goal...
issues.justification: Hockey chant 'Puck, puck' is changed to 'Goal'; the reference is partly lost and the English chant is not an exact match.

issues.source_quote: Вот это новость! Повесили тебя на собственных воротах
issues.translation_quote: Now that's news! Thou wert hanged on thine own gates
issues.justification: Inconsistent register shifts between modern 'Now that's news!' and archaic speech in the same exchange.

issues.source_quote: Я не имею права подписывать такие исторические документы.
issues.translation_quote: I have no right to sign such historic documents.
issues.justification: The joke (Bunsha's bureaucratic cowardice) is retained but 'Дорогой самодержец' later is rendered flat.

issues.source_quote: Гитлер капут!
issues.translation_quote: Hitler kaput!
issues.justification: Fine. (Minor note: no issue.)

issues.source_quote: Дер гроссер кениг, дас шведишен кенигсрейх, зандте мих.
issues.translation_quote: Der große König, das schwedische Königreich, sandte mich. Seinen treuen Diener, zu ihm, Zar und Weliki Knjas Iwan Wassiljewitsch of All Russ
issues.justification: The comic mock-German is replaced with correct German, losing the humour; the line also ends in a mid-sentence English fragment ('of All Russ') and is truncated.

issues.source_quote: Интурист хорошо говорит!
issues.translation_quote: The foreign tourist speaks nicely!
issues.justification: 'Интурист' refers to the Soviet foreign-tourist agency and is used as a joke label for foreigners; 'foreign tourist' is a weaker rendering.

issues.source_quote: Мы его в кипятке и сварили.
issues.translation_quote: So we boiled him in boiling water.
issues.justification: Redundant 'boiled in boiling water'; the dark comic phrasing is clumsy.

issues.source_quote: Так что передать мой король?
issues.translation_quote: So what I tell my king?
issues.justification: The ambassador's broken Russian is rendered as a grammatical slip, but it is inconsistent with his earlier perfect German; acceptable as imitation only if intentional.

issues.source_quote: Тоже мне, Тарапунька и Штепсель нашелся.
issues.translation_quote: Look at him, a regular Laurel and Hardy.
issues.justification: Culturally substituted reference; acceptable but Tarapunka and Shtepsel were a Soviet comedy duo, a creative substitution that is not clearly signalled.

issues.source_quote: Тамбовский волк тебе боярин!
issues.translation_quote: The Tambov wolf is your boyar!
issues.justification: Idiom 'Tambov wolf is your comrade' kept literal; the meaning is lost for English audiences.

issues.source_quote: Кличка!
issues.translation_quote: That's his alias!
issues.justification: Police slang 'кличка' (criminal nickname) is blurred; the comic effect of treating the tsar's name as a criminal alias is weakened.

issues.source_quote: Боярыня моя... На мне
issues.justification: Several omitted/blended lines (e.g. final 'Сидеть!' sequence) reduce clarity.

issues.source_quote: Ну, а это кто такой? - Муж мой.
issues.translation_quote: And they'll cure you... And they'll cure you too... And they'll cure me...
issues.justification: Sequence in the police scene is rearranged, with doubled ellipsis, making it clumsy.

issues.source_quote: Сесть я всегда успею.
issues.translation_quote: There'll be time enough for me to serve a sentence.
issues.justification: The pun on 'сесть' (to sit down / to go to prison) is lost: the tsar's answer originally plays on 'за диссертацию сесть' and 'сесть' as prison; the English drops the double meaning for the first half.
